label: Offline snapshot of Papers announced 6 Oct to 12 Oct 2026
notes: 2 lower-ranked papers were left out to keep the brief under 9 minutes.

items.title: Not Every Call Needs a Frontier Model: Per-Call-Site Evaluation of Small Language Models in a Deployed Agentic Home-Automation System
items.caveat: Evaluation is restricted to home-automation tasks using 280 cases across two Home Assistant installations and one human judge.

claims.claim: the authors report that capability varies across call sites and larger models do not always outperform smaller ones.
claims.quote: We find that capability is not ordered the same way at every site, and that larger models are not uniformly better: one 4B model is worse than its 2B sibling at grounded actuation.

claims.claim: the authors report that code generation is the only site where hosted models significantly outperform the best local model.
claims.quote: Paired testing shows the best local model to be statistically indistinguishable from both hosted models at four of five sites. Only code generation separates them, against a small hosted model (p = 0.039) as well as a frontier one (p = 0.002).

claims.claim: the authors report that selectively hosting generative sites achieves parity with fully hosted systems at 28% of the cost.
claims.quote: In a live deployment judged by a user, hosting only the two generative sites matches hosting everything (39/43 against 39/43) for 28% of the spend

items.why_it_matters: Teams deploying multi-agent pipelines can substantially reduce operational costs by substituting small or local models at simpler call sites and reserving frontier models for code generation.

items.title: BACAM: Behavior-Aware Continual Agent Merging for Multi-Turn Interaction
items.caveat: Results are confined to four specific interactive benchmark domains reported in the abstract.

claims.claim: the authors report that BACAM enables sequential agent merging without maintaining past experts.
claims.quote: We study continual agent merging, which integrates incoming experts sequentially without retaining previously merged experts.

claims.claim: the authors report that BACAM achieves an average success rate of 62.82% across four interactive tasks, beating the strongest baseline by 21.69 percentage points.
claims.quote: Across four interactive tasks - web shopping, tool use, information retrieval, and embodied interaction - BACAM achieves an average success rate of 62.82%, exceeding the strongest evaluated merging baseline by 21.69 percentage points.

items.why_it_matters: Enables combining specialized multi-turn agents sequentially without extra inference overhead or needing access to all experts at once.

items.title: End-to-End Autonomous Generation of Human Assembly Plans
items.caveat: Assembly time reductions were evaluated using a simulated robot-arm proxy rather than real-world physical human assembly.

claims.claim: The authors report that DfA-aware sequence planning reduces simulated assembly time by 35% compared to a baseline on 136 assemblies.
claims.quote: Compared with a baseline that always removes the outermost part first from Tian et al., DfA-aware sequence planning reduces simulated assembly time, measured with a robot-arm assembly-time proxy, by 35% on 136 assemblies of 5 to 30 parts.

claims.claim: The authors report that their approach selects the correct tool for 88.6% of assembly steps.
claims.quote: The correct tool is selected for 88.6% of assembly steps.

items.why_it_matters: Autonomous assembly planning from raw mesh files can enable AI agents to generate manufacturing workflows and manuals without manual engineering annotations.

items.title: How Do Agentic LLMs Decide to Call Tools? A Tool-Call Vector Shaped by Suppression
items.caveat: Analysis relies heavily on paired contrastive synthetic prompts and is evaluated on models from three specific open families.

claims.claim: the authors report finding a single causal vector that governs tool-calling decisions across multiple languages and trajectories.
claims.quote: We trace the decision to a vector, $μ_Δ$, that is both causally necessary and sufficient and generalizes beyond the discovery prompts to native multi-turn $τ^2$-Bench trajectories and verb-free requests.

claims.claim: the authors report that prompt scaffolds establish tool-call priors which analysis verbs suppress.
claims.quote: Behavioral ablations show that the scaffold establishes a tool-call prior; Transcoder decomposition then reveals that analysis verbs suppress this prior through features signaling that tool use is unnecessary

claims.claim: the authors report that this mechanistic tool-calling mechanism recurs across seven models from three distinct families.
claims.quote: the same mechanism recurs across seven models from the Qwen, Mistral, and Granite families.

items.why_it_matters: Provides a mechanistic understanding of how prompt wording suppresses or triggers tool invocation, aiding predictable agent prompt engineering and steering.

items.title: UNREAL: Unifying Retrieval and Long-Context with a Single Model
items.caveat: Evaluated only on Wikipedia and standard benchmark datasets, with abstract-level details omitted regarding general domain transfer.

claims.claim: the authors report that UNREAL requires fewer than 500K trainable parameters while keeping the backbone model frozen.
claims.quote: It adds fewer than 500K trainable parameters and leaves the backbone unchanged.

claims.claim: the authors report that the best UNREAL model substantially increases retrieval recall across HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and MuSiQue.
claims.quote: The best model raises recall from 49.1% to 73.2% on HotpotQA, from 31.7% to 60.1% on 2WikiMultiHopQA, and from 8.8% to 14.4% on MuSiQue.

claims.claim: the authors report that UNREAL enhances long-context accuracy on NoLiMa and LV-Eval by eliminating distractors before generation.
claims.quote: Applied to long-context tasks, the same selection mechanism removes distractors before generation, raising NoLiMa accuracy from 1.0% to 24.83% at its maximum context length of 128K tokens, and LV-Eval's F1 score from 49.97% to 54.66% at 256K.

claims.claim: the authors report that UNREAL reduces computation FLOPs and time-to-first-token relative to full-context inference from about 32K tokens onward.
claims.quote: UNREAL also reduces FLOPs and time-to-first-token relative to full-context inference from roughly 32K tokens onward, with larger gains as context grows.

items.why_it_matters: Unifying corpus retrieval and long-context filtering via lightweight additions to frozen LLMs could significantly reduce infrastructure complexity and compute costs.

items.title: Locate, Judge, Read: Role-Specialized Tool Agents over a Knowledge-Point Index for Open-Domain Multimodal Document QA
items.caveat: Evaluated primarily on standard benchmarks without real-world enterprise production trials mentioned in the abstract.

claims.claim: The authors report KnowForge achieves an F1 of 47.5 on M3DocVQA using Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, outperforming M3DocRAG by 11.0 points.
claims.quote: KnowForge reaches F1 47.5 on the full open-domain M3DocVQA (2,441 questions, 3,368 PDFs), +11.0 over the published M3DocRAG system and +7.1 over one-shot retrieve-and-answer on the same index and model, and 53.5 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash.

claims.claim: The authors report KnowForge attains 73.5 accuracy on MultiHop-RAG, surpassing previous published RAG and GraphRAG baselines.
claims.quote: On MultiHop-RAG it reaches 73.5 accuracy, above the strongest published RAG and GraphRAG results (71.2)

claims.claim: The authors report that consolidating search and reading tools into a single agent degrades performance by 1.9 F1.
claims.quote: merging both agents into one with all tools and twice the rounds loses 1.9 F1 because it keeps searching instead of reading

items.why_it_matters: Specializing multi-modal RAG agents into distinct locator and reader roles outperforms single-agent architectures while matching larger closed models.

items.title: RECAST: Learning to Compute the Right Context through Adaptive Evidence Routing
items.caveat: The multi-model setup involves RouterLM, CompilerLM, and AnswerLM executing generated code, introducing operational complexity and latency risks.

claims.claim: the authors report that RECAST reaches a 75.6% mean success rate across six benchmark families, surpassing the strongest large baseline by 15.9%.
claims.quote: Across six heterogeneous benchmark families, RECAST achieves a mean success rate of 75.6%, outperforming the strongest large-model baseline by 15.9%.

claims.claim: the authors report that a trained Qwen3.5-9B RouterLM beats a training-free Gemini 3.5 Flash RouterLM by 5.0%.
claims.quote: training enables the Qwen3.5-9B RouterLM to outperform a training-free Gemini 3.5 Flash RouterLM by 5.0%.

claims.claim: the authors report that RECAST beats the top baseline by an average of 15.0% across three held-out benchmarks.
claims.quote: On three held-out benchmarks, RECAST improves over the strongest baseline by 15.0% on average, demonstrating strong zero-shot generalization across tasks and heterogeneous source representations.

items.why_it_matters: Allowing RAG systems to synthesize tools and dynamically aggregate data overcomes fundamental limits of similarity-only retrieval for multi-step reasoning.

items.title: Agentic AutoRAG: RAG Pipeline Optimization through Reasoning-Driven Agents
items.caveat: Relying on LLM-judge accuracy and specialized diagnostic agents may incur high optimization-time costs not detailed in the abstract.

claims.claim: the authors report that Agentic AutoRAG matches or outperforms statistical baseline 30-trial accuracy within its first 10 trials.
claims.quote: within its first 10 trials it matches or beats the statistical baselines' full 30-trial judge accuracy.

claims.claim: the authors report that on a healthcare corpus, it achieves 77% median exam accuracy at roughly 58% of the strongest baseline's cost.
claims.quote: In its cost-aware mode on a real-world healthcare corpus it reaches a median exam accuracy of 77%, above the strongest baseline's 71.5%, at about 58% of that baseline's cost per query, and it matches that 71.5% at about 22% of the cost.

items.why_it_matters: Automating RAG pipeline optimization using error attribution can dramatically reduce tuning time and operational inference costs.

items.title: Learning to Retrieve via Reinforcement Learning in Embedding Space
items.caveat: High-dimensional embedding exploration introduces sampling noise, requiring subspace projection techniques whose computational overhead is not quantified in the abstract.

claims.claim: the authors report that RELER outperforms InfoNCE and LambdaLoss in average nDCG@10 when fine-tuning dense embedding backbones.
claims.quote: RELER consistently outperforms InfoNCE and LambdaLoss in average nDCG@10 when post-training BGE-M3 and Qwen3-Embedding backbones.

claims.claim: the authors report that adapting only the query encoder with joint rewards improves both retrieval and generation across seven QA datasets.
claims.quote: Across seven QA datasets, jointly optimizing retrieval and answer rewards improves both average retrieval performance and answer quality in RAG.

items.why_it_matters: Reinforcement learning directly on query embeddings allows organizations to optimize retrieval performance for downstream RAG tasks without re-indexing document corpora.

items.title: AECP: Artifact-Exclusive Communication Protocol for Multi-Agent Code Generation
items.caveat: Evaluations and claims are reported only from three specific benchmarks and a limited set of named models.

claims.claim: the authors report that AECP improves test pass rates by 28.2 percent and decreases wall time by 16.5 percent compared to free-form messaging.
claims.quote: AECP improves average test pass rate by 28.2% and reduces average wall time by 16.5% relative to an agent team using free-form inter-agent messages.

claims.claim: the authors report that artifact-exclusive communication stops the propagation of malicious instructions between agents completely.
claims.quote: Artifact-exclusive communication also blocks the relay of malicious instructions between agents, reducing how often they reach other agents from 95% to 0% and how often those agents act on them from 40% to 0%.

items.why_it_matters: Enforcing coordination via structured artifacts rather than conversational agent messaging can substantially boost task performance, lower runtime, and neutralize prompt-relay attacks.

items.title: Correct Code, Broken Contributions? SWE-CC: Benchmarking Repository Policy Compliance for Coding Agents
items.caveat: Policies are synthesized from developer documentation across only 12 open-source repositories.

claims.claim: the authors report that coding agents violate 43.1 percent of repository contribution policies despite generating functionally correct patches.
claims.quote: although agents produce functionally correct patches, they still violate 43.1 percent of applicable project policies, with nearly half of all violations occurring during intermediate execution steps.

items.why_it_matters: Passing unit tests is insufficient for real-world PR merges, as agents regularly violate practical project governance, git, and testing standards during execution.

items.title: CogAdapt: Cognition-informed Sparse Adaptation of Code LLMs
items.caveat: Relies on pre-collected human EEG and attention data to learn priors, and evaluations are limited to the reported benchmarks and models.

claims.claim: The authors report that CogAdapt reduces gradient-eligible adaptation parameters by 86.21% to 87.21% while improving pass@1 over matched regular fine-tuning on LiveCodeBench.
claims.quote: CogAdapt achieves the best pass@1 across both LiveCodeBench and BigCodeBench, including gains of 10.86 and 6.29 percentage points over matched regular fine-tuning on LiveCodeBench, while reducing gradient-eligible adaptation parameters by 86.21-87.21%.

claims.claim: The authors report finding consistent correspondence between human reading behavior and Mixture-of-Experts computation across Qwen and GLM.
claims.quote: Across Qwen and GLM, we find consistent correspondence between human reading behavior and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) computation.

items.why_it_matters: Selectively updating model blocks guided by human cognitive priors can dramatically cut fine-tuning parameter costs while boosting code generation benchmark performance.

items.title: TestGRAD: Evolving Test Suites via Failure Pattern Momentum for SWE-Agent Ensemble
items.caveat: Evaluation is reported only on SWE-bench Verified, with reliance on generating and executing repository tests across a multi-agent framework.

claims.claim: The authors report that TestGRAD achieves 84.2% Pass@1 with a 4-agent ensemble on SWE-bench Verified, outperforming the strongest baseline by 3.6 percentage points.
claims.quote: On SWE-bench Verified, TestGRAD achieves 84.2% Pass@1 with a 4-agent ensemble, outperforming the strongest baseline (80.6%) by an absolute improvement of 3.6 percentage points, while compressing failure-history context by over $100\times$.

items.why_it_matters: Ensembling software engineering agents with test-space optimization offers a concrete mechanism to select correct patches and boost automated issue resolution.

items.title: BoT-GRPO: Efficient Process-Reward RL for Reasoning via Bag-of-Token Aggregation
items.caveat: Requires an existing token-level reward model, which the authors note must be clean, bounded, and stable to prevent learning stalls.

claims.claim: The authors report that BoT-GRPO reaches an 80% compile rate on React front-end code generation up to 1.9x faster than standard GRPO.
claims.quote: On React front-end code generation, BoT-GRPO reaches $80\%$ compile rate up to $1.9\times$ faster than GRPO and converges faster than modern GRPO variants (GSPO, DAPO, PURE) while reaching higher final compile and VLM-judged win rates.

claims.claim: The authors report absolute Pass@k gains up to 8.1% over GRPO in half the steps on AIME mathematical reasoning.
claims.quote: On a second task, AIME mathematical reasoning, BoT-GRPO delivers absolute Pass@$k$ gains up to $8.1\%$ over GRPO in half the steps.

items.why_it_matters: Provides a critic-free token-level process supervision method that speeds up RL training for reasoning and code generation without needing complex value networks.

items.title: Event Cameras for Melt-Pool Monitoring in Additive Manufacturing: A Benchmark and a Cross-Machine Transfer Analysis
items.caveat: Benchmark uses synthetic simulated event shards and material classification remains confounded by camera band.

claims.claim: The authors report that event-spatial monitoring matches dense-frame accuracy with minimal gain from adding absolute intensity.
claims.quote: On a single-machine case study, event-spatial monitoring matches dense-frame accuracy (0.874 versus 0.863 macro-F1), and the absolute intensity that events discard adds only +0.006 under fusion.

claims.claim: The authors report that an event-rate counter recovers a high-frequency oscillation with roughly 380 times less sensor readout than frames.
claims.quote: On the NIST Additive Manufacturing Metrology Testbed (AMMT) build, a near-sensor event-rate counter recovers a raw-frame-confirmed 528.7 Hz intensity oscillation at ~380 times less sensor readout than the frame stream requires.

claims.claim: The authors report that a 93 k-parameter spiking model yields 15 times lower modeled inference energy.
claims.quote: A compact 93 k-parameter spiking model runs at 15 times lower modeled inference energy for a 0.073 macro-F1 cost.

items.why_it_matters: Event cameras can drastically reduce data rates and inference energy for high-speed melt-pool monitoring in metal additive manufacturing.

items.title: Localize Any Object in X-Ray Security Scans without Human Annotation
items.caveat: Real-world runtime performance and latency impacts are not mentioned in the abstract, and evaluations rely on reported benchmark gains.

claims.claim: The authors report that LAO-X fine-tunes SAM2 using a physics-guided synthesis and an occlusion-controlled curriculum strategy.
claims.quote: LAO-X further incorporates an occlusion-controlled curriculum strategy to fine-tune a Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2) localizer, progressively adapting it to X-ray scans with increasing object counts and overlap levels.

items.why_it_matters: It enables automated threat and object localization in industrial X-ray security scanning without requiring expensive expert human annotations.

items.title: Analysis of SWIR Imaging Detection Performance Under Adverse Environmental Conditions for Autonomous Driving Systems
items.caveat: Evaluated only on a single paired dataset (RASMD) across two detection architectures.

claims.claim: The authors report that standard RGB performs comparably or better in most scenarios, but SWIR excels in specific safety-critical edge cases.
claims.quote: Overall, RGB demonstrates comparable or superior performance in most scenarios, while RF-DETR exhibits greater robustness across varying conditions.

claims.claim: The authors report that SWIR provides clear benefits under four distinct adverse conditions.
claims.quote: This analysis reveals that SWIR offers clear advantages in four safety-critical situations, including windshield glare, water droplets on the windshield, low-contrast object visibility, and long-range vehicle detection.

items.why_it_matters: Clarifies the real-world value proposition of expensive SWIR sensors as complementary safety modalities rather than full RGB replacements.
